title.narrative: Equitable Access to SRH and Nutrition Response services for Vulnerable and Hard-to-Reach Communities of Damaturu, Nguru and Gujba LGAs of Yobe State.

description.narrative: ltpgtYobe State, particularly Damaturu, Nguru, and Gujba LGAs, continues to suffer from compounded humanitarian vulnerabilities driven by prolonged insurgency, recurrent displacement, seasonal food insecurity, and disease outbreaks. The 2025 Nigeria Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) projects that 5.1 million people in the BAY states, including Yobe state, will face acute food insecurity during the lean season, while 7.8 million individuals need life-saving assistance. In Yobe specifically, the HNO (2024) estimated that 1.5 million people will face food insecurity and nutrition crises, with global acute malnutrition (GAM) among under-5s peaking seasonally up to 8 percent. These conditions are exacerbated by limited access to services, inadequate healthcare infrastructure, and persistent threats to protection.ltbrgtTo address these critical gaps and reduce the mortality and morbidity consequences, the proposed project will deliver integrated primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health (SRH), and mental health response services across ten (10) health facilities and uses 6 mobile medical teams in Damaturu and Nguru (health) and Gujba (Nutrition) LGAs. We target 39,500 direct health beneficiaries in 6 months, prioritizing conflict-affected, displaced, and marginalized groups, including IDPs, returnees, host communities, women and girls, and persons with disabilities.ltbrgtThe health package includes OPD services, maternal and newborn health (MNH: ANC, skilled deliveries, PNC), immunization, IMCI, mental health integration (as per WHO-supported PHC capacity-building across BAY states), and outbreak surveillance and response to threats such as cerebrospinal meningitis, AWD, cholera, etc. Complementing service delivery, the initiative reinforces referral networks, implements AAP/PSEA and disability inclusion, and strengthens local health and protection systems to ensure sustainability, accountability, and resilience. ltbrgtThe intervention supports Health Sector Strategic Objectives SSO1 and SSO2 by reducing morbidity and mortality during the peak lean season, when outbreaks and service gaps are most severe. CHVs, nurses, and CHEWs will ensure timely care and continuity of service in hard-to-reach areas. The project strengthens local systems, promotes community-led solutions, and integrates protection in all activities, with deliberate inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through participatory methods and referral linkages. The project will deliver community awareness on health and mainstreaming GBV. While advocating with sectors like food security and livelihoods to address survival-based exploitation. It will strengthen local structures for community-driven solutions, integrate protection across activities, and ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through participatory approaches and referral linkages.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtRHHF will implement Health across 2 LGAs (Damaturu and Nguru). FRAD will implement Nutrition in Gujba LGA. While C3HD will implement Health in Nguru LGA.lt/pgt
